page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is a virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression. However, due to its shared CPU allocation and low core count, multi-core benchmarks are significantly limited. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores all fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block speeds at 67.19 GB/sec and write speeds at 46.3 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high memory capacity relative to its vCPU count within a budget-friendly shared-CPU tier. The resource density is advantageous for memory-intensive tasks that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core processing. It is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic text processing, single-threaded data compression, small-scale LLM inference using models under 135M parameters, and development environments. It is less optimal for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, or high-throughput static web serving.
